**Finding: deviation (Section 7.2)**

Section 7.2 runs the MFN against us rather than in our favour: before engaging another provider we must disclose and match for Vendor *any* more favourable commercial offer we receive — no product scope, no time limit, no comparison carve-outs. That is the rule's walk-away position and fails the fallback. It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

Redline (validated, preferred level): delete Section 7.2 in full. No Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so nothing beneficial to us is lost.
